title: Importance of dendritic cells in pathogenesis and therapy of conjunctival melanoma
summary: Conjunctival melanoma is the second most common malignant ocular surface disease. There are no specific treatment options for metastatic disease. The aim of this study is the role of dendritic cells.

interventions.name: BRAF mutations have been found in more than 70% of dermal melanomas and in up to 50% of CMs (Conjunctival melanoma). In our ophthalmopathological archive, an extensive amount of CM tissue is available. Here 50 of these paraffin-embedded samples are immunohistochemically analysed. We have CM tissues

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Tissue from patients with conjunctival melanoma, which is histologically confirmed.
Exclusion criteria:
Pretreatment with neoadjuvant immunotherapies, local chemotherapy or radiotherapy
